description: A fictional piton line launcher game prop for a mining scout, chunky low-poly, held level in one hand with the flat muzzle block forward. One compact muted olive painted body with wide chamfers. At the front one short thick square dark steel muzzle block with a flat face and one square dark bore opening that closes a short way in; nothing sticks out of it. On top of the body one chunky charcoal piton cassette, a flat box lying lengthwise, with a wide window on its left face showing exactly three big dark steel piton heads side by side pointing forward, each a fat square spike with a round ring eye at its back. On the left side of the body one wide flat round line spool drum about 0.11 m across, its winding one solid fat charcoal fill with a thick charcoal rim and one big dark steel octagonal hub cap, sitting flush against the body. One fat blocky olive lever block on the left flank just in front of and below the spool. One thick charcoal end block at the rear of the body. One diagonal-ribbed charcoal pistol grip raked backward with a squared charcoal trigger guard under the rear of the body. One small rectangular teal lamp window in a thick raised charcoal bezel on the left flank above the grip. The hidden right flank is plain olive shell with the right face of the cassette plain charcoal.
proportions: About 0.42 m long, 0.12 m wide and 0.2 m tall. (length : width : height = 3.50 : 1 : 1.67)
sides: everything listed as on the left flank is on the left only: the wide round line spool with its hub cap (sticks out of the flank), the olive lever block in front of it (sticks out), the small teal lamp window (flush) above the grip, and the three piton heads' window on the cassette's left face. The right flank is plain: smooth olive body, no spool, no lamp, no lever; the cassette's right face is plain charcoal. The muzzle block, the cassette, the rear end block, the grip and the trigger guard are on the centre line.
